name: Gradient Computation and Back-Propagation
text:
# Gradient Computation and Back-Propagation

Also called: Backward Pass, Differentiable Rendering Gradients

## Overview
Gradient Computation and Back-Propagation provides the mathematical and algorithmic foundation for optimizing 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) parameters by computing the derivatives of a loss function with respect to Gaussian attributes (position, scale, rotation, opacity, color, and skew). It solves the problem of efficiently propagating error signals from rendered pixel colors (or physical signals like Time-of-Flight) back to the 3D scene representation. It sets itself apart from sibling methods by defining the core differentiable chain rule for the [splatting](#23-splatting.md) rasterizer, while specialized siblings extend this to non-standard signal models (ToF), semantic features, or memory-constrained environments.

## Shared principles
The family shares the fundamental [differentiable volume rendering](#43-differentiable-volume-rendering.md) equation and the [back-to-front compositing](#2078-back-to-front-compositing.md) order. For a pixel $\mathbf{x}$, the rendered color $\mathbf{C}(\mathbf{x})$ is computed as [S1, unofficial]:

$$
\mathbf{C}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} T_k(\mathbf{x}) \alpha_k(\mathbf{x}) \mathbf{c}_k
$$

where $N$ is the number of Gaussians sorted back-to-front, $\alpha_k(\mathbf{x})$ is the opacity of the $k$-th Gaussian at $\mathbf{x}$, $\mathbf{c}_k$ is its color, and $T_k(\mathbf{x})$ is the transmittance up to Gaussian $k$:

$$
T_k(\mathbf{x}) = \prod_{j=0}^{k-1} (1 - \alpha_j(\mathbf{x}))
$$

The gradient of the loss $L$ with respect to a parameter $\theta$ of the $k$-th Gaussian is computed via the chain rule:

$$
\frac{\partial L}{\partial \theta_k} = \frac{\partial L}{\partial \mathbf{C}(\mathbf{x})} \cdot \frac{\partial \mathbf{C}(\mathbf{x})}{\partial \alpha_k} \cdot \frac{\partial \alpha_k}{\partial \theta_k} + \frac{\partial L}{\partial \mathbf{C}(\mathbf{x})} \cdot \frac{\partial \mathbf{C}(\mathbf{x})}{\partial \mathbf{c}_k} \cdot \frac{\partial \mathbf{c}_k}{\partial \theta_k} + \dots
$$

The term $\frac{\partial \mathbf{C}(\mathbf{x})}{\partial \alpha_k}$ depends on the transmittance and the accumulated color from subsequent Gaussians. The term $\frac{\partial \alpha_k}{\partial \theta_k}$ depends on the 2D Gaussian density function and its Jacobian with respect to the 3D parameters. Implementation typically involves a [tile-and-bin CUDA pipeline](#13681-cuda-tile-and-bin-implementation.md) where gradients are accumulated per-pixel into packed buffers [S1, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [ToF Gradient Computation for Gaussian Splatting](9733-tof-gradient-computation-for-gaussian-splatting.md)
Computes gradients for Time-of-Flight (ToF) signals where the rendered quantity is a quad pixel signal $\mathbf{q}(\mathbf{x})$ rather than linear color. It differs from standard RGB rendering by introducing a recursive accumulation term $\text{acc}_k^q$ that accounts for squared transmittance factors $(1-\alpha_{k+1})^2$ inherent in ToF signal integration. Choose this method when training on ToF data.

### [Gradient-Weighted Feature Back-Projection](9769-gradient-weighted-feature-back-projection.md)
A training-free method for aggregating 2D feature embeddings into 3D Gaussians. It uses the opacity-transmittance product $\alpha_k T_k$ as a [back-projection](#2450-back-projection.md) weight to assign semantic features without auxiliary neural networks. Choose this for semantic segmentation or feature-rich reconstruction without iterative [feature field](#12995-feature-fields.md) optimization.

### [SNS Backward Pass with Intermediate Variable Q](10040-sns-backward-pass-with-intermediate-variable-q.md)
Computes gradients for [Skew-Normal Splatting](#10045-3d-skew-normal-splatting.md) (SNS) by introducing an intermediate variable $Q = ARS$ to decouple rotation and scale dependencies in the 2D density function. It differs from standard 3DGS by evaluating shared auxiliary algebraic terms during rendering to enable [closed-form gradients](#7613-analytical-gradients.md) for skew and covariance parameters. Choose this when using the SNS representation.

### [Specular-Aware Gradient Gating](13432-specular-aware-gradient-gating.md)
Suppresses specular artifacts in semi-transparent scenes by modulating the gradients of the transmission color component using a local variance-based gating factor. It operates exclusively on the backward pass, stopping gradients in high-variance (specular) regions. Choose this for rendering transparent objects with specular highlights.

### [Deferred Back-propagation](13506-deferred-back-propagation.md)
A memory-efficient technique for optimizing radiance fields using full-resolution image losses (e.g., [VGG style loss](#11193-style-loss.md)). It decouples loss computation from the differentiable rendering pass by caching full-resolution gradients and re-rendering small patches. Choose this when GPU memory is insufficient for full-resolution differentiable rendering.

### Backward Pass in Half Precision
A gradient computation method using half-precision (FP16) arithmetic to optimize the accuracy-throughput trade-off. It omits block-local reductions, accumulating per-parameter gradients directly into packed `half2` buffers via `half2` atomicAdd over two-channel gradient groups, followed by a lightweight post pass that unpacks to legacy FP16 arrays [S1, unofficial]. The gradient of image $I$ w.r.t. primitive position $x_i$ is calculated as $\frac{\partial I(x,y)}{\partial x_i} = \frac{\partial I(x,y)}{\partial M_i(x,y)} \left( \frac{\partial M_i(x,y)}{\partial u} \frac{\partial u}{\partial x_i} + \frac{\partial M_i(x,y)}{\partial v} \frac{\partial v}{\partial x_i} \right)$, where $M_i$ is the primitive mask and $u,v$ are local coordinates [S1, unofficial]. This differs from standard implementations by using half precision and omitting block-local reductions [S1, unofficial].

## Background
The standard differentiable volume rendering chain rule for 3D Gaussian Splatting was introduced in the [original 3DGS](#2805-3d-gaussian-splatting-rendering-software.md) paper [Kerbl et al., 2023]. The specific implementation details of tile-and-bin [CUDA](#3671-dual-contouring-2d-cuda.md) pipelines and half-precision accumulation are described in [DiffBMP](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.22625) [S1, unofficial]. Extensions to ToF [S1, unofficial], semantic features [S1, unofficial], and Skew-Normal distributions [S1, unofficial] have been developed to address specific domain requirements.
